hints: Expand $(1 + 2x)^5$ up to the term in $x^2$ using the binomial theorem $\binom{5}{r}(1)^{5-r}(2x)^r$.
walkthrough:
Apply the binomial theorem to expand $(1 + 2x)^5$ in ascending powers of $x$:
$$(1 + 2x)^5 = \binom{5}{0}(1)^5 + \binom{5}{1}(1)^4(2x) + \binom{5}{2}(1)^3(2x)^2 + \dots$$

hints: Expand $(1 - 3x)^4$ up to the term in $x^2$ using the binomial theorem $\binom{4}{r}(1)^{4-r}(-3x)^r$.
walkthrough:
Apply the binomial theorem to expand $(1 - 3x)^4$ in ascending powers of $x$:
$$(1 - 3x)^4 = \binom{4}{0}(1)^4 + \binom{4}{1}(1)^3(-3x) + \binom{4}{2}(1)^2(-3x)^2 + \dots$$

hints: Multiply the relevant terms from $(1 + 10x + 40x^2)(1 - 12x + 54x^2)$ that produce $x^2$.
walkthrough:
Identify all product combinations between $(1 + 10x + 40x^2)$ and $(1 - 12x + 54x^2)$ that yield $x^2$:
$$\text{Terms in } x^2 = [1 \times 54x^2] + [10x \times (-12x)] + [40x^2 \times 1]$$

Sum the resulting coefficients:
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^2 = 54 + (10 \times -12) + 40 = 54 - 120 + 40 = -26$$
